Personology

Life's Zodiacs

One birthday, read four ways — the period you were born into, the Way the Moon's node put you on, the path the two make, and what happens when it meets someone else's.

How to use this

Read a birthday

Type a name. Pick a month and a day. The year is optional. Press Read it. You get the day itself first, then the week it sits in, then the deeper reading, then where the life is pointed. It is long on purpose. You are not meant to read it all at once.

The three buttons at the top of a reading

Short version turns the whole thing into plain words — a few lines about your day, about you, about you and other people, and where you are going. Press it again for the long one.

Read it to me reads it out loud and highlights along as it goes, so you can follow the words. It reads whichever version is showing, so press Short version first if you only want the quick one. The screen stays awake while it reads.

Voice lets you pick the voice. Tap it, choose from the list, press Hear it to try one. The good ones are at the top — on a phone look for a name starting Google. It remembers what you picked.

People

Press Save this person under any reading and they are kept on this device. You can also paste a whole list at once, one per line, like Ana Marchetti, 29 Nov 1988. Or bring in your phone contacts with Import contacts.

Pair

Pick two saved people and read them together — love, friendship, work, family, how close it actually gets, and what each of them brings from the family they came from.

Matrix

Everybody you have saved, read against everybody else, all at once. Easy pairs, pairs that complement each other, and pairs that run hot.

Learn

This is where you learn the system rather than just look yourself up. Astrology is small: twelve signs made from four elements and three qualities, spread over four seasons. Learn those seven words and every sign explains itself. Then take the quiz — every answer tells you why.

The Key

This is the one that is about you rather than about your birthday. A birthday says what you are made of. It cannot say where you currently are — whether you are doing well, whether you are in a ditch, what your childhood was like, whether you like yourself. So it asks.

Put your name and birthday in, then work down the questions. Most are a slider from 1 to 5. Tap a number to answer, tap it again to unanswer. Skip anything you do not want to answer — it works from whatever you give it. The boxes you type in are for you to read back — this page does not read your words or draw conclusions from them. The one thing that can is the extra pass offered under the key: its button says exactly what it sends, and nothing leaves your phone unless you press it.

Press Turn the key. You get where you are standing, then the locks — the parts of your life that are shut, each one answered by the part of your own reading that speaks to it — then what is already open, then the key itself, then the steps out of the ditch in order. It reads aloud like everything else.

It saves itself as you go, on this device only. Delete my answers really deletes them. This is the most personal thing in the app, and nothing in it leaves your phone unless you press the button that says it will.

Getting back

The round arrow in the bottom left goes back one screen. Your phone's own back button and gesture do the same thing now — one press, one screen — instead of throwing you out of the app from six screens deep. It closes whatever is open first (the instructions, the voice picker, the short version), then walks back through the tabs. When there is nowhere left to go the arrow disappears, and the next press leaves properly.

Main menu, at the top, skips all of that. One press from wherever you are and it closes everything that is open and puts you back on the screen the page opens on.

Keep it on your phone

Open the site, press Share, then Add to Home Screen. It gets an icon and opens like an app. Everything you save stays on that phone, and each phone keeps its own list. The only thing here that ever leaves it is the extra pass under the key, and only when you press its button.

Saved in this browser only — nothing leaves the file. Click a card to read it; use the × to remove.
Name, then a comma or a tab, then the date — any order: 1991-04-07, 24 Dec 1991, 24-Dec-91 or 3/14.
&
Every saved person read against every other, computed automatically. Each cell is the elemental relation between their two periods — click one to open the full pair reading.

The Key

A birthday tells you what you are made of. It cannot tell you where you currently are. Answer these and the reading gets laid against your actual life — which parts of it are shut, which parts are open, and which one opens the other.

Everything here stays in this browser. This page reads your sliders and your buttons and never reads a word you typed — the boxes are stored so you can read them back. The only thing that leaves your phone is the extra pass offered under the key, and it tells you what it is about to send before it sends it.

Whatever your phone or computer has installed. Your choice is remembered and it is the same voice that reads the birthday.

Find your Way

The Way comes from the birth year, not the day of the year. The Moon’s node travels backwards through the zodiac once every eighteen and a half years, so the same calendar date in a different year is a different Way. Put the year in and this says which one you are on and the dates it held.

All forty-eight, in one continuous run, oldest first, with the whole reading on every one. Tap a card to open it.

The cards

A reading, not a lucky draw. A reader asks a few things before dealing, because a card only means anything against a real situation — so this asks whose reading it is, what it is about, what you are going through, and what you are after. Answer by choosing; the only things you type are a birthday and, if you want the reading to carry it, a name — and neither one is saved anywhere.

Your birthday decides which cards are yours: the personality card and the soul card it gives, the number this year is running at for you, and — with a second birthday — the card the two of you make between you. The spread is dealt from that and from your answers, so the same question deals the same reading and a different question deals a different one. Nothing is stored and nothing is sent. Drawing again changes nothing, because chance is not what is doing the choosing.

Built as one self-contained file. Your people are stored in this browser's localStorage.

How this works, and what's original here

The 48 periods and their date ranges come from this project's README and are used exactly as written. The four seasons, the four elements, the three qualities, and the four quarters and twelve seven-year bands of the Grand Cycle are the frame the system is built on, used as a structure rather than as text. The correspondences are the standard personology framework: each period's sign gives its element and quality; the day of the month reduces to a number 1–9 with its ruling planet; and the day of the month also names a Major Arcana card (days 1–22 directly, days 23–31 by digit sum). Every word of interpretation — the readings, the paths, the pair profiles and the Grand Cycle — was written for this app. The cards tab is a session rather than a draw: the few questions a reader asks before dealing, then the birthday read by published method — the personality and soul card by Mary K. Greer's sum (day + month + full year as numbers, reduced by digit sum, with 19 keeping its whole chain 19, 10, 1), the personal year number from the birth month and day and this year's digits, and, when the reading is about two people, the card the two of them make between them, both birth cards added and cut back by twenty-two. The spread is dealt from that and from the answers rather than from chance, and every word of the card by card reading is this app's own. Nothing is quoted from any book, and the path names here are this app's own, not any published list.
